newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close lower on CPI expectations.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close lower on CPI expectations.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed lower on Sunday in thin trading ahead of Friday's release of October's consumer price index (CPI), which investors expect to be relatively high, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.45 percent, or 0.86 points, to 191.47 on a low all-share turnover of 47 million shekels against 80 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.49 percent to 201.17.

"Trading was very dull today and most of the activity was concentrated in the arbitrage shares (which are also traded on Nasdaq)," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.
"The market is expecting a relatively high October CPI of 0.8-1.0 percent and it seems now that the Bank of Israel will not lower interest rates in the near future," Finn said.
"The market continues to show weakness and activity is low," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities. He noted that the higher volume posted on Thursday was not the start of a new trend.
"Many shares were not traded (on Sunday) and in others activity was minimal. Our forcast is that the CPI will be around 0.9 percent, which is relatively high," Scharia added.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 0.25 percent to 144,529 on volume of 5.9 million shekels; Tadiran Ltd, which lost 1.25 percent to 1,447 on turnover of 1.9 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which fell 0.5 percent to 28,319 on volume of 1.6 million shekels.
